title: Serve one candidate population to the roster, the matrix and the retire dialog

runner_up: Honest population caps in one place: the same read answers {truncated, totals} so the roster stops reading '200 saved profiles' past PROFILE_LIST_LIMIT (profiles.ts:11) and the matrix stops presenting the newest 200 analyses as the whole field - both are open Known gaps in docs/features/candidates/README.md:1389-1415.
body:
## Summary
The Profile tab says it shows one candidate population in two projections, but it reads three: the roster reads saved profiles, the matrix reads the CV-identity population, and the archetype retire dialog re-reads the whole roster to count one archetype. Lift one population read (the landed CV-identity fold, enriched with completeness and staleness) into ProfileTab through a `useCandidatePopulation` hook and derive every projection from it.

## Description
The seam is the client: the server already shares one memo (route.ts:176-178), yet ProfileRoster.tsx:97, CandidateMatrix.tsx:77 and ArchetypeManager.tsx:74 each fetch on their own. The cost is counted:
- two different populations presented as one (profiles-only vs profiles+analyses);
- the retire dialog's count ignores analysis-only candidates in the very lane being retired;
- staleness is invisible on the matrix;
- the family answer differs between projections;
- a `dataRev` -> `reloadKey` counter exists only to re-sync the forks after a delete.

The move: `collapsePopulation` carries `completeness` and `stale` on profile rows (the candidates route passes `row.completeness` and `profileStaleness(ws)`). The new hook `useCandidatePopulation` owns one AbortController-cancelled read, an optimistic `withoutProfile` prune and a `reload`. Pure derivations: `rosterFromPopulation` (profileRosterView.ts) yields the roster's rows + StaleMap; `routedCount` yields {profiles, analyses} for the retire dialog, whose copy gains an analyses clause (one new ICU key in 4 catalogs). ProfileRoster and CandidateMatrix take rows as props and lose their fetch; ProfileTab loses dataRev. GET /api/profile is unchanged for its other readers. Technique: portable-read-definitions (one read declared once, consumed by every surface).

Collision check: r03 candidate-profile landed the identity fold this card consumes (it does not change collapsePopulation's merge rules); r04 profile-editor touches ProfileEditor/useProfileEditorFields, which this card does not write. ProfileRoster.tsx is also in this deck's slot B - the two must land in different waves.

## Flow
1. ProfileTab mounts `useCandidatePopulation()` -> one GET /api/profile/candidates.
2. List projection: `rosterFromPopulation(rows)` -> ProfileRoster (filters, sort, pager unchanged).
3. Matrix projection: rows -> CandidateMatrix (filters, lanes unchanged; a stale profile now knows it is stale).
4. Retire: ArchetypeManager asks `routedCount(rows, id)` - no fetch, both stores counted, the dialog opens with its number already known.
5. Delete in the roster -> `withoutProfile` prune + one `reload` -> every consumer sees the same population.

## Expected impact
The tab stops contradicting itself: one population, one family answer, one staleness answer, and a retire dialog whose number matches the lane on screen. Three client reads become one, the counting-dialog's pending state disappears (the count is known before the dialog opens), and the sync counter is deleted. It also gives the cap-honesty fix (runner-up) a single place to land.

## Evaluation
Claim: one population read serves roster, matrix and retire count, and they agree.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass.
After: 6 of 6.
Method: gate - node:test over candidate-population.test.ts, profileRosterView.test.ts and the mutation-proved source guard in candidateMatrixContracts.test.ts, plus the challenge integration gate (tsc, lint, i18n:check, test:unit) and the keyless e2e profile-roster spec unchanged.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture

title: Refresh every unedited stale profile from its newer CV in one counted pass
acceptance: profileStaleness(ws) for a lineage profile with a newer same-CV analysis and updated_at > lineage_stamped_at -> entry carries edited:true and updatedAt = the row's updated_at; the same profile right after setProfileLineage -> edited:false (profiles-lineage.test.ts; the equivalence oracle in profiles-staleness-equivalence.test.ts extended with the two fields and still deepEqual)

refreshRequest(entry, v2) -> {id, profile: buildProfilePayload(fields of formStateFrom(v2)), signals: {selfDeclared: formStateFrom(v2).choice, isEnrolled:false, expectedGraduation: undefined, wantsDomainChange:false, hasSubstantialExperience:false}, expectedUpdatedAt: entry.updatedAt, sourceAnalysisSlug: entry.newerSlug} - byte-equal to the PUT the editor sends when a rebuild is opened and saved unchanged (useProfileEditorSubmit.ts:67-89)

PUT answers 409 {code:'PROFILE_STALE'} for row 2 -> row 2 outcome 'changedSince', rows 1 and 3 'refreshed' (the run continues past a lost race)

PUT answers 429 for row 2 -> row 2 'throttled', row 3 'notAttempted', and the injected fetch is called no further after the 429 (the run stops honestly instead of hammering the shared profile-save bucket)
GET /api/analyses/<slug> answers 404, or a body whose analysis.v2Profile is absent -> that row 'failed' with reason 'noNewerProfile' and NO PUT is issued for it
an edited row is never PUT even when every fetch would succeed: it is reported 'skippedEdited' and listed in the review queue; an aborted signal mid-run leaves every unstarted row 'notAttempted'
premise: app/features/tools/profile/ProfileRosterRow.tsx:124-133 offers Rebuild one row at a time; ProfileTab.tsx:142 routes it to openRebuild, and for an UNEDITED profile useProfileTabDeepLinks.ts:118-120 -> openFromAnalysis (:63-83) just opens the editor prefilled with the newer v2Profile, so refreshing N stale profiles costs N editor round-trips each ending in a manual Save (useProfileEditorSubmit.ts:67-89 PUT)

the roster already filters by status: profileRosterView.ts:73-81 rosterStatus -> 'stale', rosterRows :133-138 honours filters.status, rosterFacets :107-112 offers it - the recruiter can SEE the stale set but can only act on it one row at a time

the list cannot count edited vs unedited before a run: ProfileStaleness is {newerSlug, newerAnalyzedAt} only (app/_lib/db/profiles.ts:39, query :310-332), while the divergence rule is a cheap column comparison on the same profiles row (profiles.ts:262: updated_at > lineage_stamped_at)

the server already protects a batch path: PUT re-asserts expectedUpdatedAt and answers 409 PROFILE_STALE on a lost race (app/api/profile/route.ts:281-289), and a PUT carrying sourceAnalysisSlug re-stamps lineage so the staleness clears (route.ts:295-296, setProfileLineage profiles.ts:271-284)

every PUT spawns profile_cli and draws on ONE per-IP bucket shared with the editor: PROFILE_RATE_LIMIT 60 per 10 minutes (route.ts:48, keyed profile-save at :243) - a batch must stop on 429 and say how many were not attempted, not report success

registry recruiting/candidate-identity-and-staleness technique rebuild-overwrites-manual-edits-warning, 'Bulk rebuilds are the dangerous case': skip records carrying human edits by default and report the count skipped; never run over a population not first counted; do not gate rebuilds of records with no human authorship
rollback: The store change is two extra SELECT columns on profileStaleness (no schema, no migration) and the rest is a new pure module, a new bar component and one mount point in ProfileRoster, so the commit series reverts cleanly; profiles already refreshed stay refreshed exactly as if the recruiter had rebuilt them one by one through the editor (same PUT, same lineage re-stamp).
runner_up: Retire-and-reroute: the archive dialog lists the candidates routed to the archetype and moves the saved profiles to a chosen active archetype in one pass - today the roster flags them 'retired' (profileRosterView.ts:78) and the only fix is re-routing each one in the editor.
body:
## Summary
A re-analysis of a CV marks its profile 'Newer CV', and today every such profile is refreshed by opening the editor and saving it by hand. Add a counted batch refresh to the roster: it refreshes every UNEDITED stale profile in view from its newer CV in one pass, skips the ones carrying the recruiter's edits and hands them over as a review queue, and reports each row's outcome truthfully.

## Description
The roster already knows who is stale and lets the recruiter filter to them (profileRosterView.ts:73-81,133-138), but offers only a per-row Rebuild (ProfileRosterRow.tsx:124-133). For a profile nobody edited, that rebuild is ceremony: the editor opens prefilled with the newer analysis (useProfileTabDeepLinks.ts:118-120, :63-83) and waits for a Save. Twenty re-analysed CVs = twenty editor trips.

The leap, built on the registry's bulk-rebuild rules:
- Count first. profileStaleness gains `edited` (updated_at > lineage_stamped_at, the same rule as profileDivergence) and `updatedAt`, so the roster knows before anything runs how many stale profiles in view are clean and how many carry edits.
- A bar above the table: 'N profiles in view have a newer CV - M unedited can be refreshed now; K carry your edits and will be skipped for review.' One confirm.
- `runBulkRefresh` (pure, injectable fetch, AbortSignal) walks the clean rows sequentially: GET the newer analysis, build the SAME PUT body the editor would send (buildProfilePayload over formStateFrom(v2), editor signal shape, expectedUpdatedAt, sourceAnalysisSlug), PUT. Outcomes: refreshed / changedSince (409 PROFILE_STALE) / throttled (429 - stop; the rest notAttempted) / failed (noNewerProfile or a code resolved through useErrorMessage).
- The result panel states the counts per outcome in the reader's language and lists the skipped edited profiles, each with the existing Review action (the onRebuild callback -> openRebuild's three-way merge dialog, landed by r03). No edited profile is ever written by the batch.
The roster reloads once after the run. No new route: the batch rides the existing PUT and its CAS, rate limit and lineage stamp.

Collision check: r03 landed the per-profile merge this reuses for the review queue; r04 profile-editor is writing useProfileEditorFields.ts, which this card only IMPORTS (formStateFrom) and never writes. ProfileRoster.tsx is also in this deck's slot A - the two must land in different waves.

## Flow
1. Recruiter filters the roster to Status = Newer CV (or not - the bar counts whatever is in view).
2. Bar: 'Refresh 9 unedited from their newer CV - 3 edited profiles skipped for review'. Confirm.
3. Progress: 'Refreshing 4 of 9' with a Stop (abort).
4. Result: '8 refreshed, 1 changed since you loaded the list. 3 profiles carry your edits - review each.' Review opens the existing merge dialog for that profile.
5. On 429: '5 refreshed, 4 not attempted - the save budget is spent; run again in a few minutes.'

## Expected impact
The most frequent maintenance chore on the roster (every re-analysis creates one) collapses from N editor round-trips to one counted confirm, without ever overwriting a human correction: edited profiles are skipped by default and handed over as a walkable queue, exactly the registry's bulk-rebuild rule. Outcomes are truthful per row - a lost race, a throttle and a missing analysis each say what happened.

## Evaluation
Claim: unedited stale profiles refresh in one counted pass; edited ones are never written by it; every row's outcome is stated.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over profileBulkRefresh.test.ts (injected fetch, fake 200/409/429/404 answers) and profiles-lineage.test.ts / profiles-staleness-equivalence.test.ts against a temp KP_DB_PATH, plus the challenge integration gate (tsc, lint, i18n:check, design:check, test:unit).
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract
